solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Really blessed securing refuge

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: blessed means holy
a nest is a place of refuge or retreat

explanation.surface: Someone truly fortunate has found a safe haven.
explanation.definitionFit: Both work as sentence adverbs of sincerity: 'Really, I mean it' and the answer used the same way.

clue.text: Cheer up Duke of Sussex with 20% off at posh hotel

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
the prince's name has five letters, so a fifth of it, its last letter, is cut

parts.note: Prince Harry holds the title Duke of Sussex
U is the old label for upper-class usage, so posh
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Applauding the arrival of Prince Harry at a smart hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut a fifth (the Y) from HARRY to leave HARR, add U and H, then read HARRUH backwards ('up') for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a shout of joy or approval, exactly what a cheer is.

clue.text: Next door said 'no problem' about ball coming in

indicators.note: said tells us a word is to be heard, not spelt: no, spoken as nay, is written like a horse's cry

parts.note: nay is an old word for no

indicators.note: about, here meaning surrounding, makes the first word go round the ball
the ball comes in, going inside the word for a problem

parts.note: a bur (burr) is a clinging nuisance, hence a problem
O is ball-shaped

explanation.surface: The person next door told us not to worry when their ball came over the fence.
explanation.walkthrough: NAY ('no', 'said') is heard as NEIGH; then BUR (a bur clings like a nagging problem) goes 'about' O, the ball 'coming in', to give BOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living next door is by definition the adjacent householder; the clue phrase stands for that person.

clue.text: Watched son and daughter eating tart

indicators.note: the two family letters take the pastry inside them, as if eating it

parts.note: S is the genealogy abbreviation for son
D is the genealogy abbreviation for daughter
a tart is a kind of pie

explanation.surface: A parent observes the children tucking into a tart.
explanation.definitionFit: To spy is to observe closely, so the past tense matches 'watched'.

clue.text: Boat for use in dock area is not as heavy

definitions.text: Boat for use in dock area
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flat-bottomed barge used to load and unload ships in harbour
second meaning: the comparative of light, weighing less

explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' links the two senses: a harbour barge, and the comparative of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a harbour barge for transferring cargo, and the comparative adjective means weighing less.

clue.text: Special copper's run inside following ragamuffin…

indicators.note: inside places the run letter within the chemical symbol

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
ff. is the abbreviation for 'and the following' pages

explanation.surface: A police special constable chases down a street urchin; the ellipsis carries the scene into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal, Cu. A special constable is a volunteer police officer in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruff is an untidy, dirty-looking person, which is what a ragamuffin is.

clue.text: Priest's against replacing expert teacher

indicators.note: the word for against takes the place of the word for expert within the teacher

parts.note: a professor is a university teacher
a pro is an expert, a professional
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A cleric is opposed to an academic expert being displaced.
explanation.walkthrough: Pros and cons are arguments for and against, so CON swaps in neatly for PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A confessor is the priest who hears confessions and grants absolution.

clue.text: Senior has evening meal without starter

indicators.note: the meal loses its first letter, its starter, which is a food pun

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: An older person takes dinner but skips the first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper means higher in rank, as in the upper school or upper house, so it fits senior.

clue.text: Shooting film team incorporated safety feature

parts.note: firing is shooting; fire as the noun for shooting

indicators.note: the film's title takes the team inside it, absorbing it

parts.note: E.T. is the Spielberg film
XI is a team of eleven, as in cricket or football

explanation.surface: Shooting a movie, the crew included a safety measure.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency way out of a building is a standard safety provision required in public premises.

clue.text: …tearing into slow-opening barrier

parts.note: railing at someone is berating them, tearing into them

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, the urchin is ripping through a barrier that is slow to open.
explanation.definitionFit: Railings are a fence of upright bars, a common barrier.

clue.text: Gunman finally kills retired agent at home

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word that follows
retired means withdrawn, moved back, so these letters are written backwards

parts.note: a rep (representative) is a sales agent
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A gunman finishes off an agent who has stepped back from work and stays at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a marksman shooting from a hidden position, a kind of gunman.

clue.text: Turnaround of poor community centre's captured in painting

indicators.note: a turnaround reverses direction, so the result is read backwards
poor captures, holds inside it, the central letter

parts.note: bad means poor in quality

indicators.note: centre takes the middle letter of the word that comes before

explanation.surface: A deprived community's centre has got a reversal of fortune captured on canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of COMMUNITY is U; BAD capturing U gives BUAD, and 'Turnaround of' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A daub is a crude, amateurish picture, so a kind of painting.

clue.text: Greenfly help to protect acidity level

indicators.note: the word for help surrounds the scientific measure, shielding it

parts.note: aid means help
pH is the scale measuring acidity

explanation.surface: A gardener seeks help against greenfly by guarding the soil's acidity.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly are small green sap-sucking insects, one familiar kind of aphid.

clue.text: Natterjack, rare outside of Europe for example, is protected somewhat

indicators.note: the abbreviation is protected, held safely within the other letters

parts.note: the natterjack is a European toad

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: The natterjack toad, scarce beyond Europe, enjoys some legal protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natterjack' looks like the subject of the surface, but it only supplies letters; 'outside of' takes just the first and last letters of 'rare'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to some extent or partly, the same as the adverb somewhat.

clue.text: One's exercising right to tail man pinching horse

indicators.note: to tail is to follow behind, so the right letter comes last
pinching means gripping, so the man's name holds the horse inside it

parts.note: Joe is a man's name, standing for any man
gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for horse

explanation.surface: Someone working out is entitled to follow a man who has stolen a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A jogger is a person running for fitness, so the answer is one who is exercising.

clue.text: Obtain overdue support

parts.note: get means obtain
behind means late, in arrears, overdue

explanation.surface: Collect a late payment of maintenance.
explanation.definitionFit: To get behind a cause or person is the idiom for backing them.

clue.text: Fish stuffed with medium hot chilli finishes rice

indicators.note: the fish is stuffed, filled, with the size letter

parts.note: basa is a freshwater catfish from Southeast Asia
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

indicators.note: finishes takes the last letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A recipe: stuffed fish served with a fiery chilli, finished off with rice.
explanation.definitionFit: Basmati is a long-grain aromatic variety from India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Majority nowadays hold out for change

parts.note: AD, anno domini, is the present era

indicators.note: the two words are up for change, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Most people these days hold out for change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Majority' looks like 'most people', but it is the legal sense: the age at which you become an adult.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching your majority means reaching legal adult age, so the state is grown-up life.

clue.text: Weak man's broken by diabolical spell

indicators.note: the man's letters are split open, broken, by the rearranged spell going inside

parts.note: he is a man, and the 's adds S

indicators.note: diabolical means dreadful, so the word is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A feeble man falls under a devilish spell.
explanation.walkthrough: SPELL rearranged ('diabolical') gives LPLES, which breaks up HE'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Helpless means powerless, unable to act for oneself, so weak.

clue.text: Cartier design's variable

indicators.note: a design arranges things, so the jeweller's name is laid out afresh

explanation.surface: The jewellery house Cartier's designs vary.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means unpredictable and irregular, so liable to vary.

clue.text: Crack shell collecting eggs to make a hot meal

indicators.note: the shell gathers, collects, the eggs inside it
the shell of a word is its outer letters

parts.note: O looks like an egg, so OO is eggs

explanation.surface: Crack the shells, gather eggs, and prepare something hot.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook is to prepare food by heating it, the same as producing a hot meal.

clue.text: Broadcast lecture which describes rotational force

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a talk is a lecture

explanation.surface: A broadcast lecture on physics explaining twisting forces.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent TALK and the answer are said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Torque is the twisting effect of a force about an axis, the physics term for rotational force.

clue.text: More worn out than every other time having row

indicators.note: every other letter of the word than is taken, starting from the first

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: More exhausted than ever after yet another argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel; it is a line of seats. 'Every other' picks T and A from 'than'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattier is the comparative of tatty, meaning shabby and worn.

clue.text: Clever idea almost has your leader gasping

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a wheeze is a clever scheme or trick

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone almost has a bright idea while their boss is struggling for breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheeze' has two senses; here it is the British slang for a crafty scheme, not the breathing noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheezy person breathes with a whistling, laboured sound, like someone gasping.

clue.text: Very full bag, doubts half of it needs to go in

indicators.note: the half-word must go inside the bag

parts.note: a packet is a small bag

indicators.note: half of the word doubts is kept, the second half dropped

explanation.surface: A bag stuffed to bursting, with the owner doubtful half of it will fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' points back to 'doubts': the bag word takes in that word's front half.
explanation.definitionFit: A packed-out venue is crammed with people, completely full.

clue.text: Etch verse in mind

indicators.note: in places the verse letter within the word for mind

parts.note: to mind is to care, as in 'I don't mind'

explanation.surface: Engrave a poem in your memory.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve is to cut a design into a surface, the same as etching.

clue.text: Make out contract

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hear or discern
second meaning: to get an illness

explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun for an agreement, but it is the verb for picking up an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both hearing something clearly and getting infected with a disease.

clue.text: Pancake recipe no-one used

indicators.note: used letters are worked over, reshaped into a new order

parts.note: read as 'no one': one is I, and 'no' says it is left out of the recipe's letters

explanation.surface: A pancake made without anybody following the recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I (one) out of RECIPE to leave RECPE, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A crêpe is a thin French pancake.

clue.text: Creepy crawly has Norwegians heartily rattled

indicators.note: rattled means shaken up, so the letters are jumbled
only the heart of the word is used, its outer pairs of letters dropped

explanation.surface: Scandinavians thoroughly unsettled by a crawling insect.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of NORWEGIANS, losing NO and NS, is RWEGIA; 'rattled' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: An earwig is a pincered insect, a classic creepy-crawly.

clue.text: Trying to swim 10 metres

indicators.note: letters that swim move about freely, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the figures 1 and 0 look like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: Swimming ten metres is an effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' looks like an attempt, but it is the adjective meaning annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying as an adjective means wearisome and annoying, a synonym of tiresome.

clue.text: Fleet parking's shabby- looking outside

indicators.note: the shabby word sits outside, round, the parking letter

parts.note: seedy means shabby and run-down
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A fleet of vehicles parked in a run-down spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' looks like a group of ships or cars, but it is the adjective meaning fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means swift and nimble, as in fleet of foot.

clue.text: Father lied about bringing in New Year being pleasant

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: the rearranged word takes the new letter in
about means in a confused state, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A priest lied about welcoming in the New Year to seem agreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: LIED rearranged ('about') gives IEDL, which brings in N to make IENDL.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly means kind and affable, much the same as pleasant in manner.
